title: Hardened schematic-contract fuzz + telemetry harness for constrained-decoding
creator: Leah Park
description: Build a repeatable test harness that fuzzes JSON-like contracts at the token and partial-stream level across multiple model variants, captures fine-grained decoder telemetry, and surfaces contract regressions in the Console. This is an engineering-first testbed focusing on constrained-decoding enforcement, graceful partial-stream recovery, and quantifiable contract drift metrics for rollout gating.
acceptance_criteria: Harness runs end-to-end against nightly model matrix (open and curated variants) and produces a standardized result artifact
Telemetry emits token-level decoder signals (sentinel hits, constraint breaches, partial-emit rate) to Console test-dash within 5 minutes of run completion
Fuzz corpus includes 10k+ prompts covering interleaved tool-call patterns, nested schemas, optional fields, and adversarial whitespace/tokenization cases
Constraint breach rate for known-good model/version must be <= 0.5% on canonical evaluation prompt set
Automated regression alerts created when breach rate increases by > 2x vs baseline and linked to CI/Gate
Playbook created outlining triage steps, rollback criteria, and recommended mitigations (fallback models, relaxed decoder mode, repair transforms)
test_plan: Corpus generation: combine historical failing prompts, synthetic fuzz (mutations, dropout tokens), and customer-like payloads from anonymized examples
Execution harness: run constrained-decoder in deterministic-seed mode and non-deterministic mode to measure variance
Partial-stream injection: simulate streaming truncation, late-arriving tool outputs, and network jitter to validate reassembly and sentinel recovery
Model matrix: run against runtime-1.18-compatible variants + 3 open models + 2 quantized builds
Chaos experiments: inject token corruption, rate-limited responses, and intentional early-stops to measure graceful degradation
Telemetry plumbing: add token-level events and aggregate metrics to a dedicated Console dashboard and annotate CI artifacts
steps: 1) Wire a lightweight harness repo that wraps existing constrained-decoder tests and exposes job config for model matrix
2) Define canonical canonicalization & scoring for contract adherence (structural pass/fail, soft-score for tolerated deviations)
3) Implement token-level instrumentation in decoder shim (sentinel detection, constraint-violation counter, partial-emit marker)
4) Create fuzz generator scripts (mutation strategies: drop, swap, prefix-insert, whitespace-entropy)
5) Add streaming truncation simulator that sends prefix, waits, then sends remainder, and validates reassembly
6) Hook telemetry events into Console test-dash and add alert rule for breach-rate regression
7) Land GH PRs for harness, decoder shim, and telemetry schema; run CI smoke and iterate
8) Publish runbook and short demo for QA / SRE to exercise failing scenarios
notes: Decisions: prefer a scoring-based pass/fail instead of brittle exact-match to account for model paraphrase behavior (score thresholds documented in Confluence)
Trade-offs: token-level instrumentation adds ~0.5-1% overhead to decode latency in test-only builds; we will not enable in perf-critical production builds
Observability: prefer counters + histograms (violation_count, partial_emit_latency_ms, sentinel_rate) and a lightweight event stream for triage recordings
Privacy: fuzz corpus will exclude any raw customer content; QA to validate anonymization scripts before any artifact is stored in shared buckets
Rollout plan: run nightly, promote to pre-release gate for dedicated-model rollouts, and use as part of model-onboard checklist
